props.title: Decision (2026-08-10) — intake mirrors the existing curator

text.insert: Knowledge intake is the same mechanism as today's knowledge-curator agent, extended: the three doors (past PR, discord pull, worker completion) all normalize into one proposal shape and one append path. No new agent species — the curator grows doors.

The store is maintained by one librarian-like agent. The worker writes no report: the librarian condenses the transcript and run state of everything that was done — every attempt is filed into the attempt ledger, and learnings (if any) are inferred, mapped (subject + scope), evidence-linked, and cataloged. Inference happens at intake, not at emission. When a target is picked back up, every prior attempt on it is visible.
The consolidation is live: knowledge-curator and pr-indexer no longer exist as kernel agents — the librarian is the single knowledge agent, with the three doors implemented as context variants (
condense
curation
pr_indexing
) on one role and one schema.
As built — the librarian agent
The librarian is the only knowledge agent. One shared librarian_v1 contract serves condensation, graph-safe curation, and PR indexing; deterministic jobs validate output and own every write.

text.insert: Corroboration by judgment

Corroboration is not a vote count. The librarian compares a candidate with ledger results and supplied evidence, then judges whether statements agree, contradict, duplicate, or supersede one another. It confirms, refutes, rejects, or emits a better merged statement with evidence and confidence.
Worker-finished hook
The scheduler can enqueue detached librarian condensation for each newly ended worker, but only when
--librarian-on-worker-finish
is supplied. With the default flag state, completed workers do not trigger this live hook.
As built — live intake and completed backfill

Live intake and historical backfill share the same evidence, anchoring, validation, and ledger contracts. They differ in scheduling: live work handles one newly finished packet, while backfill plans a finite manifest of historical batches and retries every non-done batch.
Live flow
A worker packet combines current worker state, typed checkpoints, a deterministic observed attempt, and transcript references.
The librarian anchors reusable claims to today's symbols and files, checks related ledger entries, and rejects unsupported or obsolete material.
Validated learnings persist as proposed records; attempt overlays and verdict counts from the live condensation job are logged but are not separately persisted by that job.
Automatic worker-finished enqueueing exists but remains disabled unless the run enables --librarian-on-worker-finish.
Present anchoring and supersession

Historical statements are validated against the current checkout before they become current knowledge. Missing anchors become stale rather than being guessed. Evidence timestamps and quality decide supersession: later or better-supported statements can replace older wording, while contradictory evidence remains available for refutation and audit.
Completed historical backfill

The run settled at 64 jobs and finished in 1 hour 53 minutes 16 seconds—under two hours—with zero validation errors. Fifteen batches needed one manifest retry. Their failures were transient codex-lb transport interruptions: seven rows explicitly record upstream websocket closes, two record upstream timeouts, and six older rows omit error text; every batch recovered on its second attempt.
Corroboration pass
57 batches remain in the original launch plan; 0 latest manifest rows are failed. Completed batches have applied 3,902 verdicts and emitted 119 merged learnings.

The one-time pass groups non-refuted learnings by exact subject, submits multi-learning groups to the librarian, and appends per-batch manifest state so a resume skips completed work. The manifest is intended as crash-safe per-wave recovery, but the implementation records done rows before writing that wave's ledger updates; a crash in that narrow window can skip unapplied verdicts. It is resumable, not transactionally crash-safe.
Discord raw puller

Discord intake is one raw source door with two ranges: full-history bootstrap or resume, and an overlapping since-yesterday incremental pull. Both write timestamped monthly JSONL with message-level evidence references; workers do not search the raw archive directly.
